sources.entry: zoxide - zoxide is a smarter cd command for your terminal.

summary.one_liner: zoxide is a smarter cd command that learns which directories you visit most and lets you jump to them with a few keystrokes.
summary.what_it_does: It ranks directories by how often and how recently you use them, then lets you jump with partial matches such as "z foo" or "z foo bar". It also supports relative paths, "z -" to return to the previous directory, and "zi" for interactive selection through fzf. Setup hooks into many shells (Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, Nushell, Elvish, Xonsh, Tcsh, and any POSIX shell) via an init command. It can import existing history from autojump, fasd, z, z.lua, zsh-z, and atuin. Behavior is configurable through init flags (--cmd, --hook, --no-cmd) and environment variables for database location, excluded directories, aging limit, and symlink resolution.
use_cases: jump to frequently used project directories quickly
replace cd with a frequency-ranked directory jumper
interactively pick a directory with fzf
import directory history from autojump, z, or fasd
navigate terminal sessions across macOS, Linux, Windows, and BSD
how_to_run: Add eval "$(zoxide init bash)" to the end of ~/.bashrc (or the equivalent line for your shell)
zoxide import z (optional, to import existing data)
notable: Learns directory usage over time and ranks matches by frequency and recency
Works across many shells including PowerShell, Nushell, Elvish, and Xonsh
Imports data from autojump, fasd, z, z.lua, zsh-z, and atuin
Configurable aging limit (_ZO_MAXAGE) and directory exclusion globs (_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS)
caveats: Interactive selection (zi and completions) requires fzf v0.51.0 or newer
Debian, Ubuntu, Parrot OS, and Raspbian packages are marked as outdated in the README, so the install script or another method is suggested there
Some shells need extra setup, such as Zsh completions loaded after compinit
